owner_confirmed_infrastructure.typical_water_depth_context: approximately 3 ft or less at pier end; tide dependent

objective: Measure local near-bottom hypoxia/stratification state with enough temporal resolution and metadata to support Jubilee forecasting and matched-control calibration.

deployment_geometry.phase_1_recommended: one near-bottom multiparameter package at the pier end, fixed approximately 0.15-0.30 m above sediment where practical and below ordinary low-water level
deployment_geometry.reason_for_phase_1: At roughly <=0.9 m total depth, the near-bottom package directly targets the low-oxygen saline layer most relevant to Jubilee onset while minimizing complexity and the risk that a fixed upper sensor emerges at low water.
deployment_geometry.phase_2_preferred: add a second near-surface package on an adjustable or surface-following mount to estimate vertical DO/salinity/temperature gradients
deployment_geometry.bottom_clearance: record exact sensor height above sediment; avoid burial, direct sediment contact, prop wash and contact with piling surfaces that create stagnant microenvironments
deployment_geometry.horizontal_offset: mount far enough from pilings/structure to sample ambient water but close enough for safe retrieval and service
deployment_geometry.reference: record sensor elevation relative to fixed pier reference plus concurrent water level/depth so apparent vertical changes are not confused with tide-driven sensor position changes

sampling.high_risk_mode: optionally increase cadence to 1-2 minutes during selected predawn high-risk windows if hardware supports it; preserve baseline 5-minute comparability
sampling.clock: UTC internally; preserve local Central Time rendering separately

power_and_telemetry.preferred: shore-powered logger/sonde with wired local data path where practical and Wi-Fi gateway for near-real-time upload
power_and_telemetry.design_rule: Wi-Fi is telemetry, not the only storage path; raw observations must be buffered locally through network outages
power_and_telemetry.surge_and_marine_environment: use GFCI-protected shore power, marine-rated enclosure/cable glands, surge protection and strain relief; keep mains voltage out of submerged hardware
power_and_telemetry.outage_policy: backfill buffered observations without rewriting observed_at; telemetry outage is missingness in availability, not a physical negative

predeployment: 24-48 hour side-by-side soak test before model admission
ongoing: cross-check against tide/depth and regional water-quality sources
postdeployment: retain raw uncorrected observations and calibration metadata

hardware_reference_classes.example: YSI EXO2/EXO2s class with optical DO, conductivity/temperature, depth and anti-fouling wiper
hardware_reference_classes.why_relevant: Supports coastal/estuarine unattended monitoring, external 9-16 VDC power, RS-485/SDI-12 style integration, internal logging and active anti-fouling; high reliability reference architecture rather than a purchase commitment.

hardware_reference_classes.example: In-Situ Aqua TROLL 600 class with RDO, conductivity/temperature and pressure
hardware_reference_classes.why_relevant: Provides the core direct variables with replaceable optical DO sensing and lower integration complexity than a full custom build.

hardware_reference_classes.example: industrial optical DO + conductivity + temperature + pressure sensors into a local logger/gateway
hardware_reference_classes.why_relevant: Can reduce hardware cost and integrate tightly with the existing desktop runtime, but anti-fouling, calibration stability, waterproofing and long-term QA/QC become the project rather than merely the electronics.

model_guardrails: No positive production weight until provenance/QC are passing and out-of-sample incremental value is demonstrated.
Near-bottom DO is DIRECT evidence only for the 437/Montrose cell and immediate vicinity; do not generalize as direct Point Clear or Fairhope bottom conditions.
Preserve sensor maintenance, calibration and fouling periods so the model cannot learn instrument-health artifacts.

In this very shallow site, depth and tide metadata are mandatory because the water column can be vertically compressed and fixed sensors can change relative position within the water column as water level changes.
A paired surface-bottom deployment is preferred only after the first bottom package is stable and serviceable.
future_expansion: Second matched package at Point Clear if the 437 deployment proves stable and informative.
Optional local current meter/ADV/compact ADCP only after DO/salinity/temperature logging is reliable.
Trigger standardized manual vertical profiles on high-risk and matched non-event mornings.
